title: Who Am I? Account Triage
description: Document your own account and repair a service account whose login shell was broken.
scenario: It is your first day as a junior sysadmin. Before you get access to anything, your lead asks you to prove you understand Linux user accounts: document your own identity from the shell, then repair a service account called svc_backup whose login shell was accidentally set to /bin/false, which breaks any interactive troubleshooting login.
symptoms: The service account svc_backup cannot be used for interactive logins
Nobody on the team has written down which groups svc_backup belongs to
Your own account details (uid, groups) have never been documented
mission: Write an account audit report to /home/intern/audit.txt containing your id output and the svc_backup passwd entry, then change svc_backup's login shell back to /bin/bash.

hints.title: Start with who you are
hints.content: Run `id` and `whoami` — `id` prints uid, gid and all supplementary groups in one line.

hints.title: Where accounts live
hints.content: Every local account is one line in /etc/passwd. Filter it with: `grep svc_backup /etc/passwd`. The last field is the login shell.

hints.title: Change the shell
hints.content: Use: `sudo usermod -s /bin/bash svc_backup` — the `-s` flag sets the login shell. Verify with grep again afterwards.

acceptance_criteria.description: audit.txt contains the output of id (uid=...)
svc_backup is a member of the backup group
